stories.title: Would even an AI disaster on the scale of Hiroshima be enough to make humankind protect itself? I fear not | Timothy Garton Ash
stories.description: It’s clear here in Silicon Valley that AI is advancing faster than humans’ ability to control it. That means even sober prophecies seem optimistic Here in Silicon Valley, the experts think that within the next couple of years we’ll see an extraordinary takeoff for artificial intelligence. “Welcome to the foothills of the singularity,” as a Stanford University friend greeted me. More prosaically, the imminent breakthrough is described as “recursive self-improvement” – the point at which AI itself trains each successive model of AI, resulting in an exponential development to something which, in many significant respects, is more intelligent than us humans. As Robert Wright puts it in his book The God Test : “Never before has the near-term future … held such a wide array of not-implausible paths for humankind that would be so wildly transformative.” But will this be heaven or hell? Heaven, says Elon Musk, who predicts “an age of amazing abundance” – although he also sees a 10-20% chance of killer robots murdering us all. Hell is more likely according to Geoffrey Hinton , one of the intellectual founding fathers of AI. “My intuition is, we’re toast,” he told an interviewer in 2023. And talking to Sebastian Mallaby , author of The Infinity Machine, a book about the quest for superintelligence, Hinton estimates p(doom) – the probability of human extinction – at 50%, “because I haven’t got a clue how to estimate the real number”. “As soon as evolution [of AI] kicks in, we’re fucked,” he adds cheerfully. But whether it’s God or Godzilla, artificial superintelligence is just around the corner. Timothy Garton Ash is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

Like murmuring the rosary, or putting our fingers in our ears and humming, this phrase is to be mumbled on repeat – “the Kardashev scale, the Kardashev scale” – a buzzy concept in tech, much favoured by Elon Musk, and precisely the thing we’ve been waiting for. The Kardashev scale is the answer both to our impending doom and our anxiety around it – and if we decide to believe in it, we won’t have to give the climate crisis a single thought until the last drip falls from the tap. This is the idea and it’s a familiar one to anyone who has watched tech billionaires take intractable, commonplace crises and decide that, among the measures and proposals in play, the vital missing ingredient so far has been them. stories.title: Democracy v the machine: the birth of the digital age and the warnings that were ignored
stories.description: Many hoped that the march of technology would usher in an egalitarian utopia – but some foresaw the threat it would pose to liberal society. Why did nobody listen? One of the stranger things about this dizzying, headlong moment in time is that it doesn’t have much of a past. Everything is about the future of this, the future of that: the future of work, the future of humanity, the future of the planet. It’s as if everyone is screaming (some ecstatically, most terror-stricken): robots are taking over the world! Meanwhile, you can’t put down your phone, unplug, delete your AI apps, tell Zoom to piss off; it feels as if you are racing toward something, and can’t stop, or look back, or think straight. But of course this weird moment in history does have a past. It comes from somewhere. It wasn’t inevitable. Things could have turned out differently. They still can. And if you look back, one thing you’ll see is that a lot of people saw this all coming. They foresaw our present when it was still the future. They thought it might turn out fabulously, a computer utopia. And they worried it might turn out disastrously. Above all, they issued warning after warning about the rise of what I call the artificial state, the replacement of the liberal democratic nation-state, the consent of the governed, with the rule of people by machines. They warned of a future in which democratic deliberation would be replaced by prediction by calculation, the public sphere would be supplanted by data-driven commerce, and drones would take the place of the demos. Why didn’t anyone listen? The new underworld is made up of innocent and well-intentioned people who work with slide rules and calculating machines and computers which can retain an almost infinite number of bits of information as well as sort, categorise, and reproduce this information at the press of a button. Most of these people are highly educated, many of them are PhDs, and none that I have met have malignant political designs on the American public. They may, however, radically reconstruct the American political system, build a new politics, and even modify revered and venerable American institutions – facts of which they are blissfully innocent. Durán is right – the antipathy towards the “tech bros” is growing. However, Durán underestimates the darkness being contemplated. The plan is for complete spatial and financial transaction control. This is not the end of democracy – it is a slavery system. Many of the people involved believe technology can dramatically extend their lifespan and they can replace most of the population with robots and automation. Now is the time to reject their limited vision with a revolution in consciousness. Thanks to Durán for the inspiration. He also offered an alternative vision in which there would be agreement for a collective objective to make AI benign by imbuing it with a love of the truth and a desire for humanity to prosper, and that governments might have to enforce this objective. Governments around the world are belatedly starting to act on AI. stories.description: Jason Arday, the youngest ever Black professor at Cambridge, was found unresponsive at an address in London. Arday had recently resigned in the midst of a plagiarism row.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany: Firefighters say Eifel wildfire now under control
stories.description: Firefighters in Germany say they have gained the upper hand in a fire that blazed for days in the Hürtgen Forest. More than 2,000 residents were forced from their homes by the flames and smoke.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?
stories.description: The Russian House stands in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it's being used to spread propaganda for Putin's Russia. Now, French authorities have said it is being used by the Kremlin for espionage.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
stories.description: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
stories.description: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
stories.description: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: How Germany's drone defense fails
stories.description: Drone defense is a priority for the German government. The latest dramatic incident involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport shows there are still substantial shortcomings.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany news: Far-right leader backs left-wing populist
stories.description: The leader of the far-right AfD in Thuringia, Björn Höcke, has offered to back populist Sahra Wagenknecht as state premier. And heat-related deaths this year are now numbered at some 12,500. DW has more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?
stories.description: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
stories.description: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
stories.description: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Unconstitutional? German intelligence to receive more powers
stories.description: German intelligence agencies have been calling for more powers in the fight against cyberattacks, terrorism and extremism. Now the government has given the go. Critics warn that red lines are being crossed.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany news: Cabinet approves intelligence service reforms
stories.description: Germany's domestic and foreign intelligence services are to get greater powers to deal with hybrid threats. Meanwhile, transport ministers are meeting to find solutions to increasingly low river levels.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
stories.description: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
stories.description: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
stories.description: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
stories.description: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
stories.description: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
stories.description: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
stories.description: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
stories.description: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
stories.description: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
stories.description: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
stories.description: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
stories.description: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
stories.description: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
stories.description: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
stories.description: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football
stories.description: Gianni Infantino is staying on as FIFA president despite growing pressure to step down. So who is football's most powerful man, why did UEFA and others turn against him, and how did he reassert his authority?
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
stories.description: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The hidden problem with small modular nuclear reactors
stories.description: Mini nuclear reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep
stories.description: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
stories.description: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: With 'rare' Paris talks, France hopes to cash in on Saudi investment programme
stories.description: Saudi's crown prince Mohammed bin Salman is in Paris to meet France's President Emmanuel Macron. The two leaders are to hold talks on a variety of topics, but first and foremost about the situation in the Middle East. For France, this is a chance to benefit from Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 investment plan. FRANCE 24's Clovis Casali is at the Elysée Palace and tells us more.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: What could new US sanctions on Iran entail?
stories.description: The US says it is preparing to announce new sanctions on Iran. It's been billed an economic D-day and is expected to add further pressure on the country's economy that's already been battered from previous sanctions and a US naval blockade. The renewed economic pressure would not be the first time the US has used economic tools at its disposal to corner Iran. But what could the new measures likely entail?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France's left fractures further as MEP launches presidential bid
stories.description: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann announced his candidacy for France's presidential election next year, joining a crowded field of far-right figures, centrists and fellow left-wingers. Hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon is planning to stand while Greens leader Marine Tondelier is campaigning while pregnant, socialist Party (PS) leader Olivier Faure and even possibly ex-president Francois Hollande are also mulling runs.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ukraine showing ‘remarkable innovation’: Kyiv ‘holding front line’ while striking Russia’s economy
stories.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Samantha de Bendern, Associate Fellow at Chatham House. Europe is taking increasingly consequential steps to support Ukraine, but de Bendern warns that they remain insufficient to address the country's fundamental vulnerability. Are Ukraine's allies prepared to actively help protect Ukrainian airspace? That debate reaches back to the earliest weeks of the full-scale invasion: even after President Biden warned in 2022 of an imminent Russian attack, Kyiv's allies ruled out enforcing a no-fly zone, fearing that direct NATO engagement could escalate into a wider war with Moscow.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Middle East live: Iran warns of a harsh response to anticipated US sanctions
stories.description: Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson on Monday warned that Tehran would respond harshly to expanded US sanctions, including measures against countries it sees as cooperating with Washington. The prospect of expanded sanctions comes after weeks of impasse, with the United States having not yet dislodged Iran’s grip on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Guinea searches for survivors after landfill landslides kill 30
stories.description: In Guinea, a landslide at a garbage dump outside the capital Conakry has claimed the lives of at least 30 people. The government of the West African country says it has mobilised significant resources to try and find survivors that may still be trapped under massive piles of waste. Less than a week ago, that same government had announced plans to close the Dar-es-Salam landfill due to dangerous conditions there.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: US sanctions 'unlikely to get Tehran to bow down' despite effect on population
stories.description: Iran has warned that Tehran would respond harshly to expanded U.S. sanctions, including measures against countries it sees as cooperating with Washington. The expanded sanctions come after weeks of impasse. The United States has not dislodged Iran’s grip on the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil passed before the war started nearly six months ago. Now, Washington is hoping the extra sanctions will bring change. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah tells us about the atmosphere in Iran, from Tehran.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m world record
stories.description: Robots exceeded human records at the World Robot Games over the weekend in Beijing's Olympic speed skating arena as China showcased its dominance in the industry. Dozens of humanoids and their human operators competed in events from athletics and boxing to football and martial arts.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Europe ramps up support to Ukraine as its US-dependent air defence runs low
stories.description: European leaders are meeting Kyiv as Ukraine holds celebrations for its 35th Independence Day. The so-called Coalition of the Willing is set to hold talks regarding support to the country, four-and-a-half years after the Russian invasion started, with the European Union having announced it was releasing over six billion euros in aid. But US support to Kyiv regarding critical air defence is still missing. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Volkswagen warns Germany's car-making industry is in jeopardy
stories.description: The CEO of the German car-making group Volkswagen is warning that the situation at the company is "more than critical". Oliver Blume is saying that ahead of meetings with the car giant's staff. He says Volkswagen and the rest of Germany's car industry are facing "the biggest upheaval in their history" due to global headwinds and Chinese competition.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Scared to death': Over 40,000 people evacuated as Nevada's Hawk fire spreads
stories.description: An additional 45,000 people have been placed under evacuation warnings in the northwestern US state of Nevada. This comes as the fast moving Hawk fire threatens the city of Reno. According to officials the fire was "human caused", but they have not detailed if it was set intentionally. Eight hundred firefighters have been mobilized to bring the blazes under control. Unpredictable winds have complicated the effort, and so far there's been zero percent containment.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France and Saudi Arabia hold talks ranging from Middle East to esports
stories.description: Mohammed bin Salman has arrived in Paris for a two-day official visit with French President Emmanuel Macron. Talks are expected to include the war in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as new energy routes to bypass the Strait. The two made an appearance at the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup, held for the first time outside of Saudi Arabia but largely funded by Riyadh.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: War-torn Ukraine celebrates resilience on anniversary of its independence
stories.description: August 24 marks the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence, and it also marks four and a half years of conflict with Russia. As European leaders meet in Kyiv, the Coalition of the Willing is set to chair a meeting with Volodymr Zelensky to discuss ways to bolster support for Ukraine, which is facing an escalating bombing campaign from Moscow.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Iran calls France's decision to expel two Iranian diplomats 'illegal'
stories.description: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday said France's decision to expel two of its diplomats was “illegal”. France's move came in retaliation for Tehran's decision not to allow two French diplomats to return to its territory.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Strategic talks in Paris show France and Saudi Arabia 'need each other too much'
stories.description: The Saudi crown prince and French President Emmanuel Macron are to chair on August 24 the first meeting of the Saudi-French strategic partnership council, and a number of agreements arer expected to be signed. Among them are a new Dragon-Ball themed amusement park deal in the Paris region and the sale of French military equipment to the kingdom. FRANCE 24's Philip Turle tells us more on what to know about the talks.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Despite ceasefire, Israeli strikes still kill in Gaza and the West Bank
stories.description: Despite a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025, violence continues in Gaza. On August 23, Israeli strikes left several people dead in the enclave, and a young boy was killed by the Israeli military in the West Bank, according to local authorities. Since the announcement of the truce, more than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has reported the launch of drones, balloons and kites towards its territory.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: European leaders rally in Kyiv to celebrate Ukraine's Independence Day
stories.description: European leaders joined President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on August 24 for official celebrations marking Ukraine’s Independence Day as Russia pushes on with its four-year-old invasion of the country. Among the guests is new UK prime minister Andy Burnham, his first overseas trip since taking office in July. FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze tells us more from Kyiv.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ligue 1: Ferran Torres saves Paris Saint-Germain against Rennes
stories.description: Paris Saint-Germain snatched a draw away at Rennes (2-2) on the opening day of Ligue 1. Ferran Torres, Paris’s new signing, came on after the break and saved the day for PSG.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Live: Ukraine backers gather as Russian attacks escalate, air defence runs low
stories.description: Ukraine on Monday hosts a meeting of its key European backers to press for air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion. The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: UEFA chief Ceferin calls for Infantino to quit, but 'not interested' in replacing him
stories.description: Aleksander Ceferin, president of the European soccer confederation (UEFA) has announced that he will not run against Gianni Infantino but warned the under-fire FIFA president that he must either quit or face a leadership challenge in March. Infantino has been mired in a crisis since the failure of his controversial – and ultimately abandoned – plan to open FIFA to private investors.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Syria says US-mediated talks addressed de-escalation, staying out of Israel-Turkey tensions
stories.description: Syria and Israel held US-mediated talks in Jordan on Sunday to defuse the crisis sparked by a strike that Israel said was aimed at preventing a Turkish military deployment. Damascus says it wants to stay out of the tensions between Israel and Turkey.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Iran discovers major new gas reserves amid war-hit energy sector
stories.description: Iran on Sunday said it had discovered more than 200 billion cubic metres of natural gas in the southern Fars province, with more than 160 billion cubic metres potentially recoverable. The find comes as the country’s energy sector faces disruption after months of US-Israeli strikes on gas facilities, oil depots and transport routes.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Crans-Montana bar owner detained over alleged domestic abuse
stories.description: The owner of a Swiss bar where a New Year’s fire killed 41 people has been placed in pre-trial detention over alleged violence against his wife, local media reported Sunday. Jacques Moretti and his wife, Jessica, are already under criminal investigation over the deadly blaze at Le Constellation in Crans-Montana.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: French centre-left candidate launches presidential bid amid divided left
stories.description: Centre-left politician Raphaël Glucksmann on Sunday launched his bid for the French presidency, aiming to unite moderate left-wing voters and challenge Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s influence ahead of France’s 2027 election. With Marine Le Pen leading first-round polls, Glucksmann is seeking to position himself as a pro-European, pro-Ukraine alternative to both the far right and hard left.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Emergency declared in Nevada as wildfire forces evacuation of 14,000 people
stories.description: Firefighters in Nevada are struggling to contain a fast-growing wildfire which has already forced the evacuation of nearly 14,000 people. A state of emergency has been called, meaning federal responders are working alongside local firefighters to try and keep it from residential areas. Details by Camille Knight.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Thousands rally in Sweden to protest climate policies ahead of general election
stories.description: Some 10,000 people rallied in Stockholm on Sunday to demand stronger action on climate change, weeks before Sweden’s general election. Climate campaigner Greta Thunberg joined the rally, as organisers accused the government of weakening emissions policies and urged politicians to act faster to meet Sweden’s climate targets.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Zelensky rejects wartime elections, saying vote would 'split' Ukraine
stories.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said that holding elections during wartime would pose a threat to the country, following a controversial call by his former defense minister to pave the way for an election. According to the latest opinion poll by the Kyiv Institute of Sociology carried out this summer, only 15 per cent of those surveyed want an election to be held at this time. Details by Eliza Herbert.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Zelensky rejects rival's call for elections, says would be 'huge risk' for Ukraine
stories.description: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has rejected the prospect of wartime elections, saying it would be highly dangerous. The remarks come in response to a call from the former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov to organise a vote, after he was fired by Zelensky last month. Analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Matthew-Mary Caruchet.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: China abruptly delays ambitious Chang’e-7 mission to find water ice on moon
stories.description: China has postponed its Chang’e-7 lunar mission, which was due to launch in the coming days and search for water ice near the Moon’s south pole, a government agency said Saturday. Officials said the mission did not meet launch conditions, without providing further details.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Greek Ithaca island hopes for big tourism boost thanks to Odyssey movie
stories.description: Greece's most famous islands have spent this year fighting to keep tourists out... with Santorini and Mykonos now capping cruise arrivals and charging steep entry fees just to manage the crowds. But on one small island, they're hoping for the opposite problem. Ithaca, the legendary home of Homer's Ulysses, is banking on a Hollywood boost, as Christopher Nolan's Odyssey draws new attention to a corner of Greece that's largely stayed off the tourist map. Story by Camille Knight.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: How will European politicians react to a summer of extreme heat?
stories.description: Europe this summer has had to face record breaking temperatures, which caused droughts, deaths, and caused devastating wildfires. While the latest heat dome has dissipated, the damage remains – the continent continues to be the fastest warming globally. Will this summer serve as a global climate reckoning? Answer with Stefan Eye-cot, professor of sociology at the University of Hamburg.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The week in pictures: a French woman in space, wildfires in Europe and the war in Ukraine
stories.description: Russian drones carry out deadly strikes in Ukraine, astronaut Sophie Adenot becomes the first French woman to spacewalk, fires rage in Belgium and across Europe, and torrential rain hits the Philippines: FRANCE 24 takes a look at the week's most striking images.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: President Zelensky says having elections in Ukraine would 'destroy the country'
stories.description: In remarks on Sunday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke out against holding war time elections. He believes it would be too dangerous for the country, that would ‘split’ Ukraine. The remarks came after his former defense minister publicly called for a vote. Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Emmanuelle Chaze.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Wartime elections would 'destroy' Ukraine, says Zelensky
stories.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks made public Sunday that wartime elections would be a "tsunami" that would "destroy the country". Kyiv has been engulfed in a political crisis over the summer, triggered when Zelensky fired popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who days later called to organise a vote.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: DR Congo, AFC/M23 group agree on roadmap for peace negotiations after Swiss talks
stories.description: Mediators representing the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 armed group and the Democratic Republic of Congo in a joint statement published Sunday said they have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks. The two sides said they had "agreed on the importance of a standardised method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations".
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Humanoid robot breaks Usain Bolt's 100m record in China
stories.description: Humanoid robots smashed sprinting records and competed in boxing, football and martial arts at Beijing’s World Robot Games, including running legend Usain Bolt's record for the 100-metre dash. The robo-athletes drew cheers from hundreds of spectators and showcased China’s growing dominance in humanoid robotics.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: French holidaymakers head north to enjoy cooler destinations
stories.description: The summer holidays in France are continuing. However, as we head towards the end of August, a trend has emerged. Destinations in the north of the country are proving more popular, due to the series of heatwaves the country has experienced this year.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Saudi Arabia asserts its dominance over Esports as MBS arrives in Paris for 'World Cup'
stories.description: Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman arrives in France for a two-day visit this Sunday. President Emmanuel Macron is hosting the crown prince for the closing ceremony of the so-called Esports World Cup in Paris… which is organised and financed by the Saudis. Analysis by Andy Miah, chair of Sciences Communication & Future Media at the University of Salford.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Presidential campaign heats up in Brazil, as Lula and F. Bolsonaro hold rival rallies
stories.description: Brazilian president Lula de Silva and his political opponent Flavio Bolsonaro pressed on with their presidential campaigns over the weekend, as both candidates held rallies in Rio De Janeiro. Top of the agenda for both candidates was crime, though the two took distinctly different approaches to the issue. Details by Camille Corcoran.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Hundreds of Gaza children join a mass swimming lesson to cope with trauma
stories.description: In Gaza, the war has upended the lives of an entire generation of children. In an effort to help them cope with the trauma of the conflict, an NGO has launched a project in Khan Younis: a huge swimming lesson that could even set a world record. Hundreds of children have gathered on the beach to learn how to swim. Story by Charlotte Hughes.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Venezuela: Two months after the quake, 12,500 people still live in temporary camps
stories.description: Two months after two earthquakes struck Venezuela, more than 12,500 people are still living in temporary camps in La Guaira. Many survivors are still struggling to come to terms with the loss of loved ones and their homes. They have been forced to adapt to precarious living conditions, exposed to the elements, with little access to medical care and humanitarian aid. France 24 reporters Herminia Fernández and Julio Uribarris visited three camps housing earthquake survivors.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Why is Saudi Arabia spending billions to become a global Esports power?
stories.description: Saudi Arabia is betting big on the global gaming industry. It's already gobbled up Electronic Arts in a $55 billion deal and the flagship Esports World Cup is now being held outside the country -- in Paris -- for the first time. This is part of efforts to diversify away from its oil and gas driven economy.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill three, including child, in Gaza Strip
stories.description: Israeli strikes in the central Gaza Strip killed three people, including a child, on Sunday, according to rescuers. The strikes came two days after a Palestinian teenager was killed by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank following a rock-throwing incident.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.description: Essendon has named Mark McVeigh as senior coach one day after a 10-point loss and worst season in club history.

stories.title: New Zealand prime minister proposes Australia-style social media ban
stories.description: The proposal marks New Zealand as the latest country to mull such a law since Australia enacted its world-first under-16s social media ban in December 2025.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Suspended sentence, $100 fine for man's naked attack on country ambulance
stories.description: Brian Charles Parfitt avoids immediate further imprisonment over the incident, which caused thousands of dollars in damage and left paramedics traumatised.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: International company's plan for multi-billion-dollar data centre in regional Qld
stories.description: A $31.9 billion hyper-scale data centre proposed for regional Queensland promises huge economic scale, while raising questions about energy demands and water security.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Matildas star receives rousing welcome in return after mother's death
stories.description: Kyra Cooney-Cross is warmly welcomed back onto the field by Arsenal fans after missing the end of last season due to her mother's illness.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Exclusive CCTV captures the violence facing Coles workers
stories.description: Exclusive video obtained by 7.30 highlights shocking scenes of aggressive behaviour towards retail workers, including a customer armed with a hammer and a security guard being thrown into a check-out machine.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: England bowler Brydon Carse under investigation over nightclub video
stories.description: England bowler Brydon Carse is being investigated over a video appearing to show him being led away from a nightclub in handcuffs by police.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 'Vector for antisemitism' platformed on podcast that received government grant
stories.description: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion was told that US conspiracy theorist, Sneako, was interviewed by an Islamic-themed podcast prior to his deportation from Australia.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Specialist ship arrives to cart SpaceX rocket from Christmas Island
stories.description: A semi-submersible cargo carrier has arrived on the remote Australian territory to ferry the SpaceX starship back to Texas.

stories.title: Specialist ship arrives to cart SpaceX rocket from Christmas Island
stories.description: A semi-submersible cargo carrier has arrived on the remote Australian territory to ferry the SpaceX starship back to Texas.
